newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zeitler warns against softening EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Zeitler warns against softening EMU criteria.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler on Wednesday warned against moves to lower the entry requirements for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) to allow as many nations as possible to take part.

"The aim is not to create 'any' euro or to push the threshold for entry so low that as many as possible can cross it -- unfortunately there are some calls for this in the media and politics," Zeitler said.

"The aim rather is to create a lasting zone of stability in Europe in which the advantages of a single currency area for companies and citizens can be fully developed," Zeitler said in an opinion piece published in Bayernkurier newspaper.

The advantages expected of EMU would only come about if the convergence criteria were taken seriously, interpreted strictly and fulfilled credibly, said Zeitler, who is also president of the state central bank of Bavaria.
